title: The First Quarter: Waking
meter: Prose (the Upanishad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Mandukya Upanishad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pada and matra, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
translation: The first quarter is Vaishvanara: its field is the waking state; its awareness turns outward; it has seven limbs and nineteen mouths; and it enjoys the gross world.
translation_hi: पहला पाद वैश्वानर है: उसका क्षेत्र जाग्रत अवस्था है, उसकी चेतना बाहर की ओर है, उसके सात अंग और उन्नीस मुख हैं, और वह स्थूल जगत का भोग करता है।

words.note: eka-una-vimshati 'one less than twenty'. Hindi उन्नीस comes from this.
From √bhuj, as bhokta in Nirvana Shatkam.

grammar: Subtractive numbers: एकोनविंशति = 'twenty minus one' = 19, exactly like Latin undeviginti. Hindi उन्नीस, उनतीस, उनचास keep this pattern.
The nineteen mouths (Shankara's commentary): 5 senses + 5 organs of action + 5 vital airs + mind, intellect, ego and citta. Compare the lists in Nirvana Shatkam.
Science link: waking awareness shows on an EEG as fast beta waves, about 13 to 30 Hz.
